artworks.title: Le Talion; La Cage; Ceux qui restent; Fortune
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on wove paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two figures in a wooded setting. The drawing shows a muscular figure playing a flute, another smaller figure, and an animal next to them. The scene is set against a backdrop of dense foliage, suggesting a natural environment. The drawing has intricate shading that gives depth and texture to the figures and the surrounding vegetation. The style of the drawing is reminiscent of classical themes often explored in mythological representations.

artworks.title: Ménages d'artistes; Le Maître
artworks.medium: 5-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: The image shows detailed illustrations of flowers in different stages of bloom, featuring shades of peach, white, and yellow, set against a muted green background. The color palette is mainly soft pastels. The flowers are arranged diagonally across the image, with peach and yellow blossoms at the top right, white and peach blossoms in the middle, and white blooms at the bottom right. The text "Théatre Libre" is located in the upper left corner.

artworks.title: Annabella ('Tis Pity She's a Whore)
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: The image shows a woman seen from a three-quarter view from the back, emphasizing her upper body and head. She is standing, with her head turned slightly to the side. Her facial features are outlined, with short hair framing her face. She is wearing a flowing garment, possibly a dress, with flowing lines indicating light fabric. Her left arm is extended towards another figure in the background, who is reaching towards her. The backdrop is dark, contrasting with the lighter figure of the woman. The image includes handwritten text, including the title "Annabella," names, and addresses, possibly suggesting it is an advertisement or announcement.

artworks.title: La Belle au bois dormant
artworks.medium: collotype on light brown wove paper
artworks.dimensions:
plate: 12.5 x 21.9 cm (4 15/16 x 8 5/8 in.)
sheet (program closed): 17.1 x 27.5 cm (6 3/4 x 10 13/16 in.)
sheet (program opened): 17.1 x 54.8 cm (6 3/4 x 21 9/16 in.)
artworks.description: The image is a sketch of a person lying on their side. The person is reclining on a surface with their head on a pillow, body horizontal. The face is turned slightly towards the viewer, with closed eyes and soft waves of hair. They are wearing a long, patterned garment with a belt, and a circlet around their head. Their feet are covered with shoes or slippers featuring buttons or ornaments. The background is plain textured paper with no additional elements.

artworks.title: L'École des veufs; Au Temps de la ballade
artworks.medium: inkless embossing (gaufrage) on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a vintage theater program. The program includes information such as the name of the theater, titles of plays, names of individuals credited with roles, and event details. The layout is simple with text in varying font sizes. The program is in French and printed in monochrome. It provides insight into theatrical culture from the late 19th century.

artworks.title: La Dupe; Son petit coeur
artworks.medium: embossing (gaufrage) on brown wove paper
artworks.description: This is an image of a program or leaflet for theatrical performances. The paper features an embossed figure, with typed text indicating the season (1891–1892) and naming the theater as "Le Théâtre Libre". The program lists performances "La Dupe" and "Son Petit Cœur" along with role and performer details. The design and typography reflect a late 19th-century style.

artworks.title: Nell Horn
artworks.medium: 4-color lithograph with embossing (gaufrage) on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a theatrical poster for "Nell Horn" at Le Théâtre Libre. The image features a silhouette of a person with arms outstretched, rendered in yellow against a vibrant red background that blends into the silhouette. The poster includes text with details about the play, such as the title, characters, theater company, date, and other participants. The layout is vertical with information primarily on the right side and the silhouette figure stretching across the center. The color scheme uses shades of red, yellow, and beige.

artworks.title: Dancing Nude
artworks.medium: transfer lithograph in brown on light brown wove paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: The image depicts a full-body drawing of a nude male figure in a classical style. The figure is in a dynamic pose with one leg raised and a lean forward. His head is turned to the side, partially hidden by his arm covering it. The facial features focus on the muscular structure, and the hair is curly and short. Flowing lines around the figure suggest movement or wind, with a stylized tree in the background. The background consists of swirling lines and shading hinting at movement and depth, with faint landscape elements in the distance.

artworks.title: Morituri
artworks.medium: lithograph in red-brown on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an abstract scene with a complex and dynamic composition. It includes a horse and rider in the foreground, along with swirling forms and faces. A wooden guillotine stands tall over a crowd of heads and bodies. The setting is tumultuous with stormy skies and elements suggesting motion and disorder. The style features exaggerated figures and expressions, with various text elements included in the design. The intricate line work and shading add depth to the piece.

artworks.title: Brand
artworks.medium: lithograph in green-brown and red on wove paper
artworks.description: The image depicts two illustrations. On the left, there is a drawing of a person kneeling in red-tinted water, with one hand raised to comb through long dark hair. A faint face is visible in the water behind them. On the right, another person is shown from the back, holding onto a second person who is looking upward. The background has swirling brushstrokes and a mountain landscape, conveying a dynamic and slightly chaotic atmosphere. Text overlays include the title "l'œuvre Brand," references to Henrik Ibsen’s play "Brand," and a list of cast members with some bold, stylized fonts.

artworks.title: La Victoire
artworks.medium: lithograph in brown on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: The image depicts a person in a side profile. The person is looking to the left, with their torso slightly turned away from the viewer. They have a slender face with distinct cheekbones and styled-up hair. The person is draped in a large cloth or cape, covering their shoulders and extending downwards. There are no visible jewelry or objects being held. The background features swirling, cloud-like shapes and muted tones.

artworks.title: Une Mère; Brocéliande; Les Flaireurs; Des Mots! Des Mots!
artworks.medium: lithograph in orange on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a magazine cover. The cover features text and an illustrated figure. The dominant colors are warm orange hues on a beige background. On the left side, there is text and an abstract human face with flowing hair. On the right side, there is a tall figure extending an arm. The figure is set amidst a fluid background that hints at nature or abstract elements. The style is reminiscent of early-20th-century art publications, with intricate linework and decorative elements commonly found in Art Nouveau design.

artworks.title: Une Journée parlementaire
artworks.medium: photolithograph in black on wove paper
artworks.description: The image shows a man standing in profile, smoking a cigarette next to a door. He is balding with a beard, wearing formal attire. He leans against the wall, looking downward. Another character's face is visible through a small window in the door. Text in the image likely denotes theatrical roles. The background is simplistic, drawing attention to the central figures and text.

artworks.title: La Brebis; Le Tandem
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on light brown wove paper
artworks.description: The image depicts two individuals on sepia-toned paper. The primary figure, a woman, is shown from the waist up facing slightly left with her right hand on her hip. Her facial features are outlined with attention to detail. She has light-colored hair in an updo and wears a large, detailed hat. She is in a jacket with large buttons and visible cuffs. The second figure, a man, is depicted from the chest up, possibly behind a window with shutters. He has facial hair and combed-back hair, wearing a dark outfit. The background includes foliage painted with loose strokes. Printed text on both sides mentions titles and names related to theater or literary works.

artworks.title: L'Inspecteur Général Revizor
artworks.medium: photorelief on wove paper
artworks.description: The image shows a drawing of five male figures depicted from the waist up. The men are in close proximity, appearing to be engaged in a conversation. The figure on the left wears a bowler hat and a coat, sporting a mustache and angular facial features. Next to him, two men are wearing military-style caps; they have beards and their expressions are partially obscured by the beards and shading. The central figure has distinct facial hair and a large mustache, and he is dressed in a uniform with noticeable buttons. He appears to be gesturing with his hand. The two figures on the right also wear hats and have long beards, with one seemingly looking at the central figure. The background is a beige-colored paper with printed text filling the right and left margins, detailing information about a play titled "L’Inspecteur Général 'REVIZOR'."

artworks.title: A Bas Le Progrès!; Mademoiselle Julie; Le Ménage Brésile
artworks.medium: 4-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a painting of a marching band procession. The scene depicts a group of individuals wearing blue coats and red hats, marching in formation. In the foreground, musicians play brass instruments such as the horn and tuba, leading the procession. The background shows the continuation of the marchers along a path edged by a building. To the left of the image, there is text listing a theatre program with titles such as "A Bas Le Progrès!", "Mademoiselle Julie", and "Le Ménage Brésilè". The text appears to frame the image as part of a theatrical playbill or advertisement. The artwork features colored pencil or crayon application, with a pointillist or stippling effect in its color. This is in the style of Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec.

artworks.title: A Bas Le Progrès!; Mademoiselle Julie; Le Ménage Brésile
artworks.medium: 4-color lithograph on laid paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: This painting features a marching band parade. The image shows a group of musicians in uniform, wearing bright blue coats and red hats, marching in formation. In the foreground, musicians are seen playing brass instruments enthusiastically. The composition captures the movement and energy of the parade as it travels along a street lined with simple structures. The use of bright colors and bold outlines creates a lively and somewhat festive atmosphere.

artworks.title: A Bas Le Progrès!
artworks.medium: 3-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a man with a rifle breaking a tool. The image features a man in a white shirt and blue trousers, breaking a wooden object with a rifle. The text around the image includes the phrase "A BAS LE PROGRÈS." The drawing has a soft, sepia-toned background, with the man's clothing color and the rifle in muted shades. The artist's signature and some additional text are present. The overall tone of the drawing conveys resistance or protest against advancement or change.

artworks.title: Theater Program for "Boubouroche" and "Valet de coeur (Jack of Hearts)"
artworks.medium: color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: The image shows an aerial view of a canal with a barge docked, buildings in the distance, and a bridge crossing over the canal. The scene is painted in bold brushstrokes with warm earth tones dominating the color palette. Two figures are walking on a path on the left, with a bridge and distant hills in the background. The image is framed by text, resembling a page from a theatrical program.

artworks.title: Theater Program for "Boubouroche" and "Valet de coeur (Jack of Hearts)"
artworks.medium: color lithograph on laid paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: This is a painting of a canal scene with a barge and two figures. There is a wooden barge with a red, green, and white painted pattern on its stern. In the foreground, two figures in dark clothing are on a yellow-colored surface. To the left, a bridge and other structures are in the background. The piece uses muted colors focusing on form and texture, with variations of color for depth. This is in the style of Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec.

artworks.title: Grand-Papa; Si c'était
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on wove paper
artworks.description: The image depicts an artistic pencil sketch showing three figures. Two figures are standing, while one is lying on the ground. The standing figure on the left is depicted with the upper half of the body, leaning forward slightly with arms crossed over a rounded abdomen. The facial features of this figure are simplistic with minimal detail, and the person appears to have short hair and wear a long, loose-fitting garment. The standing figure on the right is shown from head to toe with hands resting on their hips. This figure also has simplified facial features and appears to have short, wavy hair, wearing a loose garment and socks extending above the ankles. The third figure is lying on the ground in a reclining position, with a partially visible face showing closed eyes, positioned horizontally in relation to the standing figures. The person's clothing is undefined but suggests a garment suitable for lying down. The background is plain, indicating an illustration rather than a realistic setting. Accurate text elements on the left describe a theatrical performance titled "Grand-Papa," by Claude Berton, associated with 'Le Théâtre Libre,' listing the cast and other performance information for the 1894-1895 season.

artworks.title: La Belle au bois rêvant; Mariage d'argent; Ahasvère
artworks.medium: 5-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: The painting depicts individuals seated in a cafe or restaurant setting. Some men are reading newspapers at booths. The interior has red seating and yellow walls. There are pitchers and glasses on a table. A program for theatrical or musical events is on the right listing three performances and names of characters and performers. The style is similar to Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec's lively scenes of Parisian nightlife.

artworks.title: Le Devoir
artworks.medium: 4-color lithograph on wove paper
artworks.description: The image depicts three men in a bar or pub setting. The first man wears a blue suit and hat, facing the bartender. The second man, the bartender, wears a sleeveless black vest, a white shirt, and has a mustache. The third man, leaning against the bar, wears a brown coat and a cap. The bar counter with bottles is visible in the background, along with pale yellow walls. The style suggests it is associated with Le Théatre-Libre's 1892-1893 season.

artworks.title: Le Devoir
artworks.medium: 4-color lithograph on laid paper [proof before letters]
artworks.description: This is a painting of a bar scene with three individuals. The figures are depicted in a bar-like setting, with one leaning against the bar, another standing with a hand gesture, and a third seated. They are dressed in early 20th-century fashion. The bar counter has bottles and a glass. The background includes a shaded archway, and the color palette consists of greens, browns, and yellows. The style is sketchy and outlined, reminiscent of Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec.
